BOYCOTT IS NOT ALWAYS ABOUT HATE.

Sometimes, boycott is a way of standing up for yourself. A way of saying..

"My dignity is not something you can simply disrespect, step on, then expect me to continue giving you my money."

And this is where the @kahfeveryday  incident gets interesting.

And there's another issue brands often underestimate..

People don't need to boycott you forever for a boycott to hurt your brand.

They simply need to STOP CHOOSING YOU.

If a customer who previously bought Kahf starts buying another brand, that competitor now has an opportunity to become the new habit.

That's where the real commercial risk lies. That's whay you're seeing BadLab brands EVERYWHERE.

So I wouldn't measure this only by asking.."How many products were boycotted?"

I'd look at more into...
Brand sentiment before vs after the incident, Customer trust, Purchase intention, Social sentiment. Search interest, Repeat purchase behaviour, Retailer/distributor reaction ( MOST IMPORTANT  DATA), and lastly..Competitor switching...Whether the controversy becomes part of the brand's long-term narrative.
